name: Gold's Gym Venice
who: The original Gold's Gym, founded on Venice Beach in 1965 and now on Hampton Drive.
why: Known worldwide as "the Mecca of bodybuilding" — Arnold Schwarzenegger and generations of champions trained here, and it still draws lifters on pilgrimage.
reach: IG 31K on the location account @goldsgymvenice1; global Gold's Gym brand account is 455K (verified 2026-08)
takeaway: Go early, train among the pilgrims, and study how the old guard structures a session.

name: Muscle Beach Venice
who: A free, city-run outdoor weightlifting platform on the Venice boardwalk, open since 1963.
why: The original open-air "Muscle Beach" where Southern California's bodybuilding culture was born; still open daily and a required stop for fans of the sport's history.
reach: No single official account; covered constantly across bodybuilding and travel content, exact reach not tallied (verified open 2026-08)
takeaway: Free and open to all — claim a spot on the platform where 1970s-80s bodybuilding first performed for the public.

name: Bev Francis' Powerhouse Gym
who: An independent hardcore gym on Long Island founded by IFBB legend Bev Francis, billed as "the East Coast Mecca of bodybuilding."
why: Trains top NPC and IFBB competitors — Chris Bumstead used it during a 2022 Olympia prep stretch — and keeps a coaching-floor culture built around Francis's own competitive record.
reach: Facebook 59K; X (@eastcoastmecca) 17.4K; Instagram follower count not confirmed (verified open 2026-08)
takeaway: Seek out the coaching-floor culture Bev Francis built from her own competitive record — Chris Bumstead once prepped here.

name: MetroFlex Gym (Original)
who: The original MetroFlex warehouse gym, running since 1987, marketed as "the gym that built Ronnie Coleman."
why: Home turf of 8x Mr. Olympia Ronnie Coleman and 2x Arnold Classic champion Branch Warren; raw, no-frills training culture that spawned a national gym chain.
reach: Instagram @originalmetroflexgym; open and active, follower count not confirmed (verified 2026-08)
takeaway: Skip the polish — this raw, no-frills warehouse floor is the culture that built Ronnie Coleman.

name: MetroFlex Gym Long Beach
who: MetroFlex's Southern California outpost, a hardcore bodybuilding and powerlifting gym near Long Beach.
why: Carries the MetroFlex chain's coaching culture and equipment standard into the dense SoCal bodybuilding scene.
reach: Instagram @metroflexlbc; open, follower count not confirmed (verified 2026-08)
takeaway: Expect the same MetroFlex coaching culture and equipment standard as the original, dropped into the dense SoCal bodybuilding scene.

name: Zoo Culture
who: Bradley Martyn's flagship gym, now based in Encino after outgrowing its original Los Angeles location.
why: One of the most-followed physical gyms online, built around Martyn's influencer-driven strength culture and a constant flow of content creators.
takeaway: A members-only social club built on Bradley Martyn's brand — go see how online fame becomes a real training culture.

name: Iron Addicts Gym
who: The gym CT Fletcher built his brand around; still running under new ownership after Fletcher's exit from day-to-day operations.
why: Years of viral "It's a lifestyle!" training footage made this a global reference point for hardcore strength culture, and the location keeps that identity.
reach: Active social presence; follower count not confirmed this pass (verified open 2026-08)
warning: CT Fletcher is no longer associated with day-to-day operation of this location; the gym continues under different ownership.
takeaway: Come for the hardcore strength-culture identity CT Fletcher's viral footage built, even though he no longer runs the floor.

name: Dragon's Lair Gym
who: A 12,600 sq ft hardcore training facility owned by 7x 212lb Mr. Olympia Flex Lewis, with 115+ machines and dedicated power racks.
why: Gives fans a direct line to a reigning Olympia-class champion's personal training approach, with regular pro visits and seminars.
reach: Instagram @the_dragons_lair; open, follower count not confirmed (verified 2026-08)
takeaway: Check the seminar schedule — regular pro visits give you a direct line to Flex Lewis's own training approach.

name: Quads Gym
who: A 40,000 sq ft hardcore bodybuilding gym on Chicago's North Side, running since 1976 and nicknamed "Land of the Giants."
why: A Midwest bodybuilding institution with decades of old-school iron culture; voted a top-10 gym in America.
takeaway: Old-school iron culture since 1976 — earn your spot in what regulars call the Land of the Giants.

name: Armbrust Pro Gym
who: Josh Bryant's strength-and-physique hybrid gym, known for a dedicated leg room with eight-plus Olympic power racks.
why: Trains IFBB pros and elite strength athletes and serves as a serious destination for hardcore leg and powerlifting-style training.
takeaway: Hit the dedicated leg room with its stacked power racks — where IFBB pros go for serious leg work.

name: Alphaland
who: A 19-acre, three-gym bodybuilding and powerlifting complex outside Houston, opened in 2021 and nicknamed "Disneyland for bodybuilders."
why: The newest mega-mecca in the sport, drawing a younger generation of competitive lifters with unmatched scale and variety of training zones.
reach: Widely covered in bodybuilding press as a top US gym; exact follower count not independently verified this pass
takeaway: Treat it like a day trip — three gyms, courts, a sauna and a cafe built by a YouTuber into one compound.

name: Temple Gym
who: The gym built by 6x Mr. Olympia Dorian Yates, now relocated to Birmingham's Jewellery Quarter.
why: Defined the 1990s "blood and guts" high-intensity training era; still draws UK and international lifters tracing Yates's method.
reach: Instagram @templegymuk; relocated but active, listings current as of July 2026 (verified 2026-08)
takeaway: Study the high-intensity 'blood and guts' method Dorian Yates built here — brief, brutal sets, not marathon sessions.

name: Oxygen Gym
who: A Kuwait City gym owned by Bader Boodai, where 2x Mr. Olympia Big Ramy was discovered and developed early in his career.
why: A key node in the Gulf's fast-growing pro bodybuilding pipeline, visited by touring IFBB pros training in the region.
reach: Historic association with Big Ramy (1M+ personal IG); gym's own account reach not independently confirmed this pass
takeaway: Expect heavy competition-prep traffic — this is the anchor gym of Kuwait's outsized competitive bodybuilding scene.

name: Gold's Gym Harajuku
who: A 24-hour Gold's Gym flagship in Tokyo's Harajuku district, Japan's best-known bodybuilding-focused commercial gym.
why: The training hub most associated with Japan's competitive bodybuilding scene and its growing IFBB presence.
reach: Open 24 hours; follower count not confirmed this pass (verified open 2026-08)
takeaway: Head down to the hardcore Classic Gold basement floor, the part of this 24-hour club athletes actually seek out.

name: MetroFlex Gym Japan
who: MetroFlex's first Asia location, in Saitama Prefecture, importing the chain's rare equipment and hardcore culture.
why: A pilgrimage stop for Japanese and touring lifters seeking MetroFlex's specific old-school machines and floor culture outside the US.
reach: Instagram @metroflex_gym_japan; open, active as of mid-2026 (verified 2026-08)
takeaway: Seek the same rare MetroFlex equipment and hardcore culture as the Texas original, now on the ground in Japan.

name: Doherty's Gym
who: Australia's best-known hardcore bodybuilding gym group, anchored by its 24/7 Melbourne City location.
why: The default training base for Australia's competitive bodybuilding and powerlifting scene for decades, open every day of the year.
takeaway: Open every day of the year — this has been the default base for Australia's competitive lifting scene for decades.

name: Choopan Classic Gym
who: A 130-plus-machine gym Mr. Olympia champion Hadi Choopan built in his home region of Iran.
why: A symbol of Iran's rising bodybuilding pipeline and Choopan's effort to give back to the community that produced a world champion despite travel barriers to Western training hubs.
reach: Covered widely in bodybuilding press through 2025-2026; gym's own social reach not independently verified this pass
takeaway: See what a Mr. Olympia champion built for his own community when travel to Western training hubs wasn't an option.

name: Ironberg (São Paulo)
who: A 24-hour flagship of Brazil's Ironberg chain, self-described as Latin America's largest bodybuilding training center.
why: Anchors Brazil's large, IFBB-heavy bodybuilding scene inside one of the region's biggest and busiest training floors.
takeaway: Expect one of the region's biggest, busiest training floors anchoring Brazil's IFBB-heavy bodybuilding scene.

name: FIBRA MAX
who: "The Athletes' Factory," billed as the largest weight-training gym in Europe, opened in 2024 with 400-plus machines and dumbbells.
why: A new-generation European mega-gym putting Spain on the map for large-scale strength and physique training.
reach: Described in press as Europe's largest weight-training gym; follower count not independently verified this pass
takeaway: See the scale for yourself — 400-plus machines make this the largest weight-training gym in Europe.
